title: New map structure: operating systems, hardware, and niche tools

steps.intro: Built from 2,785 real posts (all of r/TrueOpenSource, plus r/opensource, r/selfhosted, r/linux, r/coolgithubprojects, r/SideProject and the r/ClaudeAI TV and keyboard threads). Of the 1,880 posts about a piece of software or a device, today's map fits 28%. The new structure fits 91% (r/TrueOpenSource alone: 95%).

steps.headline: Go ahead with this structure: 6 areas, 27 categories, 317 groups?
steps.changed: Apps for everyday life (9 categories, including new Games and gaming) · AI (AI apps; Coding agents and their tools; Building with AI) · Operating systems (Computer systems and Linux distributions, sorted by who they're for: leaving Windows or Mac, gaming, privacy, old computers, home server…; Desktops and customization; Under the hood: kernel, drivers, running Windows apps; Phones and tablets) · Hardware and devices (TVs and streaming boxes: home screens, removing ads, replacing the TV's system, like tv-vibehack, Homestead and skippy-tv; Computer accessories: keyboard and mouse tools vs Razer, Logitech and Corsair apps, OpenRGB, BIOS; Home, network and gadgets; Making things: 3D printing, electronics, radio) · Developer tools (Writing code; Hosting and running code; Databases and data; Building blocks for apps) · Self-hosting and system tools (Home servers; IT security; Computer utilities).
steps.notice: All 123 current groups keep their addresses; 41 move to a better category; 194 are new. New groups' projects are candidates until a check confirms their licenses and facts. Full write-up: docs/research/taxonomy-v2.md.

steps.headline: How should the top level be organised?
steps.today: 11 flat categories on the home page.
steps.problem: 27 categories in one flat list is a wall; too few hides operating systems and hardware.

options.label: 6 areas, categories inside
pros: Operating systems, Hardware and Developer tools each get a clear front door.
Each area page stays a short list.
cons: One more click to reach a category.

options.label: About 15 flat categories
cons: Developer and hardware topics crowd the everyday ones.

options.label: Today's 11 plus 4 new
cons: Operating systems and hardware stay buried.

steps.headline: What should the home page show first?
steps.problem: Most visitors want everyday apps; builders and Linux people want their areas fast too.

options.label: Everyday first, areas below
pros: Normal visitors see what they came for.
A second row of area tiles (AI, Operating systems, Hardware, Developer tools, Self-hosting) is one scroll away.

options.label: Six area tiles first
cons: Everyday apps become one tile among six.

steps.headline: Show all 317 groups, or hide the 20 thinnest until a project lands in them?
steps.problem: Near-empty groups look unfinished; hiding too many drops coverage.
steps.proposal: Hiding the 20 thinnest keeps coverage near 90%. Showing only busy groups would drop it to about 79%.

options.label: Hide the 20 thinnest
cons: A few real posts have nowhere to land until those groups fill.

steps.path: Groups like 'API clients' or 'Coding agent memory'
steps.headline: Groups with no paid rival just list the open projects, with no 'Replaces' line?
steps.today: Every group lists closed apps it replaces.
steps.problem: Most developer tools, utilities and device hacks don't replace a paid product; forcing one would be made up.
steps.proposal: Those groups are named by the job and list open projects only. Where a closed rival exists (Postman for API clients), it still shows.

steps.headline: Add an honest tag on hardware groups saying the device itself stays closed?
steps.problem: A TV launcher is open source, but the Samsung TV it runs on isn't; the page mustn't imply otherwise.
steps.proposal: A short tag on those groups: 'Runs on a device you already own; the device itself stays closed.'

steps.headline: Put coding-agent tools (memory, usage meters, MCP servers) under AI rather than Developer tools?
steps.problem: It's the busiest topic in the posts (150), and it sits between AI and developer tools.
steps.proposal: Under AI, as 'Coding agents and their tools', next to AI apps and Building with AI.

steps.headline: After you approve the structure, fill the new groups the same way as before?
steps.today: New groups have candidate projects only, not yet checked.
steps.problem: Unchecked licenses would break the 'only real open source' promise.
steps.proposal: Builders verify each candidate's license with the checker, write plain summaries, set Easy/Advanced setup and devices, add checklists for the new groups, and I show you a deck of the new pages before anything goes live.
